title.narrative: Women driving resilience in agriculture and rural areas, UN WOMEN
Women driving resilience in agriculture and rural areas, UN WOMEN

description.narrative: Project aims at removing structural barriers, by introducing time and labor-saving technologies, innovating sources of financing, enabling women to be better prepared to cope with challenges, to improve their livelihoods and socio-economic situation of their families in rural areas.

Projektet syftar till att undanröja strukturella hinder, genom att introducera tids- och arbetsbesparande teknik, innovativa finansieringskällor, vilket gör det möjligt för kvinnor att vara bättre förberedda på att klara utmaningar, att förbättra deras försörjning och socioekonomiska situation för sina familjer på landsbygden.

The overall objective of the contribution aims at removing structural barriers, by introducing time and labour-saving technologies, innovative sources of financing, enabling women in BIH to be better prepared to cope with the challenges, including change-related risks, improving their livelihoods and socio-economic position and the lives of their families.
The proposal includes two outcomes: 1) mainstreaming gender consideration into policy making, institutional budgeting, planning, programming and monitoring processes to create an environment conducive for women farmers, women-led agri-businesses, cooperatives, associations and networks. 2) establishing integrated approach to address problem pf women from rural areas limited access to economic opportunities. This will be done in the view of strengthening resilience to climate change risks both from the supply and demand. More specifically, outcomes are expected to be achieved through implementation of the three complementary Outputs.
When it comes to measurable quantitative impact, the project's goal is to capacitate the total of at least 200 women who will benefit from safeguarded or new jobs and improved livelihoods. Addressing both supply and demand side, the project will on the supply side mobilize private sector agriculture finance to improve the access to commercial funding sources for at least 50 women. On the demand side at least 180 women farmers/entrepreneurs will receive training modules on identifying agricultural practices to enhance environmentally sound and sustainable agricultural production. It is also expected that over 50 government officials and policy makers relevant for identifying and addressing gender inequalities in agriculture and rural development sector will be trained.
Moreover, the project is also expected to strengthen the country's entrepreneurship climate and overall agribusiness industry with a particular focus on engagement of women and their integration into structured agricultural value chains. Another significant market development which this project is expected to generate concerns the evolution of agricultural finance in BiH, especially the financial products and services accessible by women borrowers.

Outcome 1 Enabling Environment Strengthened: The project achieved full targets under this outcome. Two entity-level agricultural subsidy programmes were adopted with gender-responsive financing criteria, marking a major institutional breakthrough. Capacity-building for 40 officials (71% of target) and structured policy dialogues enabled ministries, gender mechanisms, and civil society to collaborate effectively. Over 115,000 people were reached through communication campaigns, and 36 media features exceeded visibility targets. Public discourse began shifting from perceiving rural women as passive beneficiaries to recognizing them as active innovators and economic leaders within resilient food systems. These results reflect deep systemic progress in gender-responsive governance.
Outcome 2 Womens Economic Position Improved: This outcome also achieved full targets, reaching 310 women entrepreneurs with improved access to finance, technology, and climate-smart investments. Through evidence-based studies, dialogue with banks, and partnership with agriculture ministries, 56 women agripreneurs accessed public subsidy schemes (112% of target). The pilot financing programme introduced gender-sensitive criteria into subsidy mechanisms, creating lasting institutional change. Nine women-only Farmer Field Schools (FFS) trained 183 participants across six regions, improving technical knowledge, leadership, and digital skills. Networking platforms connected 90 women across value chains, fostering collaboration and market visibility. Collectively, these efforts have enhanced womens financial confidence, digital literacy, and productivity paving the way toward a more inclusive, climate-smart rural economy.
Further, several unexpected yet positive results emerged. The introduction of gender-responsive ESG frameworks within banks signaled a transformation in how financial institutions perceive gender equality as part of good governance rather than social compliance. Additionally, the project stimulated young womens participation in agriculture and encouraged womens retention in rural communities, reversing trends of out/migration. The projects communication campaign significantly exceeded outreach expectations, contributing to a shift in societal perception of women in agriculture according to the partner.
The project success lies in its systemic approach integrating policy reform, capacity building, financial inclusion, and communication. According to the partner embedding gender criteria in public subsidies and banking practices, it achieved structural transformation rather than temporary empowerment. The project also supported positioning Sweden as a leading donor for gender equality and rural development.
In summary, the third interim period demonstrates that the project met targets and in several areas exceeded expectations. It produced measurable policy shifts, empowered hundreds of rural women through knowledge and finance, and influenced both institutional and public narratives around gender equality in agriculture. While procedural and macroeconomic challenges persisted, partnerships and adaptive management ensured that project managed to proceed despite the initial delays.
